profiles.title: The Crucifixion
profiles.subject: Scriptural scenes

overview.text: St. Nicholas parish’s Holy Friday account places the Crucifixion within Christ’s Passion, death, and burial. It explains His death through His voluntary love and obedience, and through the defeat of death that the Church celebrates at Pascha.

sourceRefs.locator: Introduction; Commemoration of Great and Holy Friday, paragraphs 2–6

overview.reason: Necessary concise account of a modern published explanation; full prose reproduction rights have not been established.

blocks.text: The Crucifixion type shows Christ nailed to the Cross, with His mother and other witnesses alongside. Blood and water from His pierced side recall John’s Gospel. The skull below refers to Golgotha and, in the tradition reported by the parish, Adam’s grave.

sourceRefs.locator: Icons of the Commemoration of Great and Holy Friday, Crucifixion description

blocks.reason: Necessary concise account of a modern published explanation; full prose reproduction rights have not been established.

blocks.text: The selected Russian panel is attributed to Dionisius and dated 1500. The parish distinguishes the Crucifixion from related Holy Friday images: the Extreme Humility combines the dead Christ and the tomb, while the Lamentation concerns the preparation of His body for burial.
